# Independent audit: single-fiber enlargement reserve and cap response

2026-09-25. PASS for Sections1--5 of
`candidate be4d9f84e764ef2a`
as read in full. This audit does not cover companion examples still
being prepared in separate files.

The reserve polyhedron uses exactly the non-self anchored representation
vertices and the fixed target-fiber facet normals. Testing those finitely
many normals is sufficient because target fibers are polytopes. Testing
only extreme anchored representations is sufficient because each support
constraint is linear in the coefficients. Canceling a target self-weight
is valid, including after the chosen source fiber is enlarged. At the
changed target, all non-self combinations remain in the old fiber and
hence in the enlarged one. Thus the iff feasibility statement really
keeps every measured fiber and the complete integer base fixed.

For the reserve-facet move, retaining the normal list retains the trivial
recession cone. Uniform boundedness and Hausdorff convergence follow.
Any sequence of newly added points converges, along a subsequence, to
the moved old facet; its strict reserve neighborhood therefore absorbs
all new points for sufficiently small parameters. This local condition
does not require the other anchored constraints to be strict.

The derivative is the facet's one-sided outward trace, not an arbitrarily
chosen closed-cap indicator at a coincidence. An outside-facing coincident
cap receives the added strip; an inside-facing one receives none. A purely
base-dependent cap either receives the whole strip or none, including
closed equality. Fubini on facet patches, with polyhedral edge-neighborhood
remainders, yields the stated area coefficient. The dimension-one case
uses endpoint counting and gives the same formula.

For the regular circuit test, both extra hypotheses are used: a genuine
two-sided threshold derivative of positive size S, and zero facet-area
intersection of the cap boundary with the moving facet. They justify
adding the threshold and body derivatives without omitting a min/max
branch. The normalization kappa_j proportional to rho_j/S_j is correct:
it makes sum rho_j dot_b_j=0 and equalizes all cap derivatives to their
kappa-weighted facet trace. Exact affine threshold changes preserve the
whole-plane circuit cover. The separately assumed fixed slack covers
retain their gaps, so the displayed upper derivative for maximum depth
follows after dividing by M+tA+o(t).

The theorem is correctly restricted to an already polytopal family and
specified regular covers. It supplies neither a polytopal unrestricted
minimum nor a reserve facet with favorable sign. No nonzero centroid
or BM deficit is treated as establishing that missing premise.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
